messages:
Priya: Heads up — saw a sharp drop in prefix/KV cache hit rate in prod after yesterday's runtime release (v2.3.4). Dashboard: https://dash.internal/redwood/cache/hitrate (us-west). Profiling shows lots of cold starts for identical prompts. Anyone else?

Aisha: Yup. Alert at 08:12. Hit rate for chat completions fell from ~76% -> ~41% across the last 6h. Latency p50 up ~18ms, p95 up ~70ms. Severe for short prefixes.

Tom: Did we change tokenizer or prompt shaping in model-adapter/llm-client updates? That would explain key mismatch.

Javier: We merged model-adapter PR #4123 which bumped tokenizer from v1.12 -> v1.13. v1.13 applies NFKC normalization and splits certain unicode ligatures differently. Also a tiny system prompt patch landed from product (added a single "context: user_profile" line).

Priya: Profiler trace (attached) shows KV cache misses line up with the deploy window for that PR. Also seeing more KV evictions — same logical prefix arriving as different keys.

Emma: If tokenization changed, prefix hashing will diverge. Do we include tokenizer version in the cache key today?

Tom: Not consistently. Current key is basically hash(model_name + raw_prefix + user_id). We only do minimal whitespace collapse in a few code paths. No tokenizer/version pinning.

Aisha: That's likely the root cause. Two quick mitigations: 1) rollback the tokenizer bump on canary, 2) update key generation to include tokenizer version and optionally system_prompt hash.

Javier: Agree, but including system_prompt in every key means PM edits will invalidate caches broadly. Maybe include sys prompt hash for model-scope keys but omit it for short user-prefix keys, or make it a gated flag.

Priya: Proposal sketch:
- Canonical normalizer pipeline for keying:
  1) unicode NFKC
  2) collapse whitespace to single spaces, trim
  3) normalize curly quotes/dashes to ascii
  4) strip ephemeral tool fields (tool.trace_id, __debug)
- Key template: "model|tokenizer@<ver>|sys@<hash?>|userprefix@<sha256(prefix_normalized)>"
- Two-layer approach: user-prefix key (no sys hash) + protected key that requires sys & tokenizer match

Tom: Example pseudocode for normalization and keying:
```python
def norm_prefix(s):
    s = unicode_nfkc(s)
    s = re.sub(r\"\s+\",\" \"\", s).strip()
    s = s.replace('\u201c','\"').replace('\u201d','\"')
    s = s.replace('\u2014','-')
    j = try_parse_json(s)
    if j and 'tool' in j:
        j['tool'].pop('trace_id', None)
        j['tool'].pop('__debug', None)
        s = json.dumps(j, separators=(',',':'))
    return s

key = f\"{model}|tokenizer@{tokenizer_version}|sys@{sha256(sys_prompt)}|p@{sha256(norm_prefix(prefix))}\"
```

Aisha: Include tokenizer_version so we never mix encodings. If we do in-place tokenizer upgrades, we need migration: backfill popular prefixes or schedule warmups.

Priya: We tested async warmup where router schedules low-priority requests to prime KV for top-N prefixes. Backfilled top-1k prefixes overnight and reduced cold-starts ~32% in canary.

Javier: For prod rollout plan:
- Always pin tokenizer_version in key.
- For one release window, run a compat mapping that tries to map old-tokenizer token joins -> new key for most popular prefixes.
- If PM changes system prompt, have a checklist: canary + opt-in warmup job + key pinning.

Emma: Any perf cost from extra normalization and hashing on the hot path?

Priya: Microbenchmarks: full normalize + two SHA256s adds ~0.4ms median. Mitigations: use murmur64 for short prefixes (<64 chars) and do normalization in router worker thread before handing to GPU path so kernel selection isn't delayed.

Tom: Note: runtime v2.3.4 also changed KV memory layout (compact vs scatter) which increased key object churn and rehashes. That likely amplified eviction rate during the deploy window.

Aisha: After rolling tokenizer back on canary and pinning tokenizer in the key, hit-rate recovered from 41% -> 73% in ~45m. No kernel rollback required.

deploy-bot: rollback model-adapter v1.13 -> v1.12 completed at 2024-04-17T09:02:31Z (deploy-id: dpl-7731). :white_check_mark:

infra-bot: snapshot us-west1 prefix-hitrate BEFORE=0.41 AFTER=0.73 (45m). KV-evictions/sec dropped 3.2x. Memory delta: +0.9% due to extra in-flight warmups.

Priya: Action items:
- Javier: open RFC for canonical normalization + key template, include migration rules and compat window checklist.
- Tom: add tokenizer_version to router key generation and introduce feature flag for sys_prompt hashing.
- Ops: schedule async warmup job to run for top-2k prefixes after tokenizer or system-prompt changes.
- Emma: run microbench perf test to validate murmur64 fallback and worker-thread normalization latency.

Priya: Treat tokenizer bumps as migration events from now on. I'll draft the RFC and include a canary + warmup + key-pinning checklist. Thanks everyone.
